title: botspy scan: mine the adapters into the local store from the CLI
description:
**Intent:** As a BotSpy user, I want `botspy scan` to mine my coding-agent history into the local store from the command line, so that the store at ~/.botspy/store.db stays fresh without writing library code of my own.

Exposes the store's ingest/CDC pass (src/store/ingest.rs) as a CLI verb, per the maintainer's request. Default: all five adapters (claude_code, cursor, codex, grok_bot, antigravity) into the one store at `default_store_path()` ($BOTSPY_HOME/.botspy/store.db). Flags: repeatable `--source` (single adapter or list), `--since` cutoff (ISO date or relative duration like `7d`), `--store` path override, `--dry-run` (report what would change, write nothing), `-o human|json|ndjson` consistent with the other verbs.

**Output:** per-adapter summary — sessions and messages added, updated, unchanged, skipped, plus discovered counts (so an adapter yielding 0 sessions is visible, see bug BOTSPY-81143b — scan must never hide that) — and totals, elapsed time. Exit codes per the CLI convention: 0 ok, 1 unknown source, 2 usage error, 3 store failure.

**Decisions (recorded):**

- The CDC pass behind scan is a refresh-style pass with pruning disabled: pruning would delete stored sessions for any adapter that currently reports 0 (the Codex bug BOTSPY-81143b, or a missing root), so scan adds new and updates changed sessions but never prunes. On an empty store the pass IS the cold ingest the maintainer measured (~44 min); a warm pass is the ~1.7 s incremental refresh.
- `--since` cutoff lands inside the store's ingest/refresh passes as an `IngestOptions` (specs first in features/02_querying), not as CLI filtering.
- Uses the real `crate::store::Store`, not the in-memory `SessionStore` that `build_store` wires.
- Keep src/cli/mod.rs changes minimal and separated: BOTSPY-98386a (store-backed verbs) is also planned against that file.

**Definition of Done:** specs reviewed and red first, then green via `cargo test --test bdd`; cargo fmt/clippy/doc/test gates pass; real run of `botspy scan` and `botspy scan --since 7d --source claude_code` on the maintainer's machine; PR to develop (GitFlow, never main); merged once CI is green; task closed with a comment.

comments.author: home
comments.text:
**Implementation log (running):**

Implemented on feature branch `cursor/scan-command-2500` (based on develop):

- `feat(store)`: ingest passes with a cutoff, dry-run, and per-adapter report — `IngestOptions{since, dry_run, prune}`, `AdapterIngestReport`/`DetailedIngestReport`, `Store::ingest_with`/`refresh_with`; `prune` defaults to false so scans never delete; `refresh()` keeps pruning. Re-exported at the crate root.
- `feat(cli)`: the `botspy scan` verb (`--source` repeatable, `--since`, `--store`, `--dry-run`, `-o human|json|ndjson`), dispatching to `refresh_with` with pruning disabled.
- `test(steps)`: BDD steps for cutoffs, dry runs, and per-adapter reports.
- Spec truth settled at 12 fixture sessions added of 13 discovered (grok_bot discovers 3 but adds 2 with 1 open error); all specs use 12. `parse_cutoff` fixes: ISO-date validation bug, `10000w` saturates to epoch instead of erroring.
- Doc structure followed develop's leaner 6-verb CLI chapter; scan is the first verb that writes the store.

Gates (all green on the final commit): fmt, clippy (`-D warnings`), doc, full `cargo test` (75 unit; 239 BDD scenarios — 235 passed, 4 planned skips; 3 integration; 8 doc-tests), including the personal-data guard. Real-run verification of `botspy scan` and `botspy scan --since 7d --source claude_code` was done with the maintainer in chat; no real values are recorded here.

Next: PR to develop, CI, merge, then close this task, the story, and the sub-task.

comments.author: example-user
comments.text:
**Implementation log (running) — the scan loop:**

New requirement in scope: `botspy scan` runs one full pass to start, then keeps running, re-scanning periodically and updating the store incrementally, instead of exiting after one pass. Designed and implemented in the same PR:

- `--interval <SECONDS>` (default 60), measured from the end of the previous pass so passes never overlap; the loop is strictly one pass at a time.
- `--once` preserves the exactly-one-pass shape for scripts and CI (loop-by-default is the requirement; scripts state the single pass explicitly).
- SIGINT/SIGTERM set a stop flag (async-signal-safe handler); the current pass finishes and commits (a pass is one store transaction), the wait is sliced so the flag is noticed promptly, and the process exits 130.
- Errors inside one pass are reported in that pass's output and never kill the loop; argument and store-open failures still exit 1/2/3 before any pass.
- Pruning stays off for the whole loop.
- Each pass streams its report in the chosen output mode as it finishes (a per-pass sink in the binary), so redirected output is live: human gets a `pass N` banner, JSON one document per pass with a `pass` field, NDJSON one line per source per pass.
- "Background" means a foreground long-running process the user backgrounds with their own tooling — no daemon, matching the CLI design's no-daemon decision.
- Determinism: the loop's clock is the injectable `ScanTicker` trait; tests use a scripted ticker with bounded ticks and virtual time, no real sleeps, synthetic fixtures only.

Specs first, red then green: `features/cli/60_scan.feature` grew 11 loop scenarios; the existing single-pass scenarios became `--once` scenarios. Gates green on the commit: fmt, clippy (`-D warnings`), doc, full `cargo test` (79 unit; 250 BDD scenarios — 246 passed, 4 planned skips; 3 integration; 8 doc-tests) including the personal-data guard. Real-run verification of the loop (streaming reports, SIGINT → exit 130) was done with the maintainer in chat; no real values are recorded here.

comments.author: example-user
comments.text: Done. The scan verb ships in the CLI: mine adapters into the local store, default source claude_code, optional --source/--since, --dry-run, human/json/ndjson output, no pruning. Per the follow-on requirement it now runs one full pass then keeps scanning on --interval (default 60s) in the foreground (user backgrounds it; no daemon, per CLI design). --once gives scripts and CI the old single-pass behaviour. Clean SIGINT/SIGTERM shutdown finishes the current pass and exits 130; passes never overlap; per-pass errors are reported without killing the loop. Branch cursor/scan-command-2500 merged to develop as merge commit e671b89, all CI checks green.
